title: Canonical polynomial log chart, characteristic maps and coordinate ideal
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative ring and $P$ a commutative monoid. With the logarithmic structures and strict local rings of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-trf-log-etale-restriction-stalk-comparison, def-trf-strict-henselization-local-ring-maps] and the polynomial ring of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], define the following canonical constructions. For $\alpha:P\to(C,\cdot)$ and $r\in\mathbf N$, the structural map $P\times\mathbf N^r\to C[t_i:i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)]$ sends $(p,n)$ to $\alpha(p)\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$. For a geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, the global-section germ into the strict henselization is induced by its structural morphism and the canonical affine global-section identification. For a log structure $M$ on $X$, transport its ideal of log nonunits along the canonical strict-local comparison to obtain an ideal $I_M(x)$ of $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,x}$. A chart section $c:P\to M(X)$ has characteristic map $p\mapsto[\operatorname{germ}_x(c(p))]$. For $w:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}C[t]$, let $t_i(w)$ be the germ of the actual polynomial variable, let $K(w)=\{i:t_i(w)\in\mathfrak m_w\}$, and let $L(w)$ be the ideal spanned by the $t_i(w)$ for $i\in K(w)$. The finite set $K(w)$ can be empty. These are the existing polynomial chart constructions, relocated without any change of name, type, or body.
